issues.description: Field 'numberOfLoopings' of class 'RollerCoaster': the UML in the problem statement declares this attribute as private (visibility '-' in the UML), whereas the solution implementation declares it as protected ("protected int numberOfLoopings"). This discrepancy leaves students uncertain whether subclasses are expected to access the field directly (protected) or use the public getter (private), and which artifact (UML or code) reflects the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent between the UML/problem statement and the reference implementation. Preferred action: change the solution's field to private (private int numberOfLoopings) and keep the existing public getter getNumberOfLoopings(), so subclasses access the value via the getter. Alternatively, if direct subclass access is intended, update the UML/problem statement to show protected visibility. Document the chosen convention in the problem remarks to avoid student confusion.
